    last_obj = stripped.rfind("}")

from llm_router import LLMRouter, Model, Provider, RouterProfile

    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "item": {"type": "string"},
        "quantity": {"type": "integer"},
    },
    "required": ["item", "quantity"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}

_PLAIN_BODY = json.dumps(_EXPECTED)

def _query_with_body(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, body_text: str):
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY_1", "inventory-assurance-value")
    response_body = openai_success_response(text=body_text)
    with (
        ScriptedHTTPServer(
            port=0,
            routes={
                ("POST", _CHAT_PATH): [
                    ScriptedResponse(
                        status_code=200,
                        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                        body=response_body,
                    )
                ]
            },
        ) as server,
        patched_openai_sdk(
            forced_base_url=f"{server.base_url}/v1",
            disable_sdk_retries=True,
        ),
    ):
        router = LLMRouter(
            RouterProfile(model=Model.DEEPSEEK_V3, provider=Provider.OPENROUTER),
            temperature=0.0,
        )
        return router.query(
            "Count the pallet jacks visible on the shelf.",
            response_schema=_SCHEMA,
        )

@pytest.mark.verifies("REQ_STRUCTURED_TEXT_OUTPUT[revision==2]")
def test_string_json_reply_validates_against_dict_schema(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Plain and fenced string replies yield the same dict under a dict schema."""
    plain_response = _query_with_body(monkeypatch, _PLAIN_BODY)
    fenced_response = _query_with_body(monkeypatch, _FENCED_BODY)

    assert plain_response.data["parsed"] == _EXPECTED
    assert fenced_response.data["parsed"] == _EXPECTED

structured.explanation: This test will not catch SM-2D3D81E7, and I couldn't run the checker (shell access was denied). The public API only ever hands _parse_json_object a string. The executor passes result.output_text, and the prompted adapters pass string candidates. Every string first goes through _extract_json_payload. That function returns the slice from the first "{" to the last "}" whenever the text contains an object. So text like [{...}] is reduced to the inner object before json.loads runs. Decoding a string can therefore only give a dict, an error, or a list with no objects in it. The mutant's [{...}] branch can only be reached by passing a Python list directly, which the public API never does. Through the public API, the mutant behaves the same as the original. The test pins that a one-item list reply yields the plain object {"item": "pallet jack", "quantity": 3} under a dict schema. Catching the mutant needs a unit test that imports the internal schema module, which the rules forbid.
